newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian government weighs suing tobacco firms.
newsitem.headline: Canadian government weighs suing tobacco firms.

text.p: Canada's Health Minister David Dingwall said on Wednesday he was considering possible lawsuits against tobacco companies to recoup the costs of treating people who suffer from illnesses caused by using tobacco products.
"I am looking at that possibility, but I will need the assistance of others in that particular process. We are not at a decision at this point in time. It's still under examination," he told Reuters.
Dingwall gave no details of how he might proceed.

Several states in the United States have sued tobacco companies for similar damages, leading to talks about a possible settlement by the tobacco companies which could result in $300 billion in payments to the states over 25 years.

The Toronto Globe and Mail reported that the provincial government of British Columbia has vowed to introduce legislation to make tobacco companies more responsible for smoking costs, estimated at C$1 billion.

The newspaper a study by the federal department Health Canada said Canadian society lost $15 billion Canadian ($11 billion U.S.) in 1991 from a combination of the medical costs of treating smoking-related illnesses, residential care, worker absenteeism and fires.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent owned by B.A.T Industries Plc of Britain.
The second biggest player, Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, is owned 60 percent by Rothmans Inc and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Rothmans Inc is a unit of Rothmans International Plc, which is owned by Swiss luxury goods holding company Cie Financiere Richmont AG.
Third place holder RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
American cigarettes are also sold in Canada. ((Reuters Ottawa Bureau 613-235-6745))
